incidents.victim: Web servers globally (government, education, media, technology, gaming)
incidents.vector: Exploited known one-day vulnerabilities in internet-facing IIS and Linux servers, then used AI-assisted tooling to deploy the custom SPECTRE cross-platform backdoor, a Linux kernel rootkit, and BadIIS malware with bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver EDR evasion.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos documented a mature intrusion ecosystem monetizing access via SEO fraud and data theft, with a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs; the actor integrates agentic AI into exploitation, payload generation, and persistence workflows.

incidents.victim: N-able Passportal customers (2,500 MSPs, ~165,000 SMBs)
incidents.vector: A design flaw in the Passportal cloud password manager's browser extension trusted any web page's postMessage requests, letting a malicious website or injected iframe request and receive access and refresh tokens carrying the vault's secret key.
incidents.impact: Any passing website could have enumerated and stolen every credential and TOTP in a customer's vault, with an MSP compromise cascading to downstream clients; patched a day after disclosure, though server-side decryption and lack of end-to-end encryption leave residual risk. No known exploitation.

incidents.victim: Banking customers in Mexico (and some in North America, Europe)
incidents.vector: Spam email delivers a zip disguised as an invoice containing decoy documents and a repurposed legitimate file-management app that DLL-sideloads the Grandoreiro loader, which runs extensive anti-analysis and sandbox checks before fetching the payload.
incidents.impact: The 12-year-old banking trojan resurfaced with a heavily protected loader, continuing to steal banking credentials via keylogging, screen sharing, and remote control despite a 2024 law enforcement takedown.

incidents.victim: Afghan government and telecommunications organizations (and attempted Indian government targets)
incidents.vector: Phishing lures impersonating telecom and government tools deliver the new Patchcord and Sheetcord backdoors, using browser-shortcut hijacking for persistence and Google Sheets for covert command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Acronis confirmed compromise of an Afghan Telecom (AFTEL) IT officer and an Afghan subsidiary of an international company, with data theft used to build further phishing lures; parallel attacks on Indian defense, foreign affairs, and air force targets were not successful.

incidents.victim: Wildberries (Russian online marketplace)
incidents.vector: Ukraine's GUR, working with a pro-Ukraine civilian hacker group, disrupted customer service, contact centers, and payment infrastructure alongside drone strikes on a Wildberries warehouse.
incidents.impact: The cyberattack degraded Wildberries' service and payment systems; analysts assessed the impact as additive to the kinetic drone campaign and largely a psychological/propaganda effect.

incidents.victim: CareCloud (electronic health record provider)
incidents.vector: A hacker accessed one of CareCloud's AWS environments from March 10-16 and exfiltrated data during roughly eight hours inside an EHR environment.
incidents.impact: 3,756,469 people had personal information, Social Security numbers, ID numbers, credit/debit card data, and medical and insurance information exposed; no group claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Latvia Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an internet-exposed CSDD system, accessing historical payment-receipt data dating back to 2008; several mandatory cybersecurity requirements had not been met.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 1.2 million people (two-thirds of Latvia's population) and 200,000 businesses was stolen, including ID numbers, license plates, and addresses; the supervisory board resigned and the agency chief announced his departure amid a national-security controversy.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (water, energy, manufacturing, chemical, food/agriculture) using Siemens S7 PLCs
incidents.vector: Threat actors use internet scanning services to find exposed Siemens S7 Series PLCs and deploy AI-generated Python exploitation scripts (using the snap7 library) disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to read/write PLC memory, configuration, and ladder logic over the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE, and EPA warned of an 'active threat' conducting persistent reconnaissance and capability development to pre-position for operational effects; the advisory is unattributed but follows recent Iran-linked intrusions at dozens of water utilities across at least 12 states.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government agencies (Ministry of Digital Affairs)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-language operator ran a near-autonomous multi-agent AI framework (built on OpenClaw and Hermes agentic tooling) using up to eight subagents across 12 attack waves to crack credentials, find and exploit vulnerabilities, and install backdoors, coordinated by a Bayesian scoring parent agent.
incidents.impact: Researchers at Dream documented the first purported near-autonomous AI attack on a nation-state; Taiwan's MODA confirmed abnormal AI-driven attacks on government agencies in July, including exfiltration of personnel records and web-app backdoors.

incidents.victim: PTC Windchill/FlexPLM customers (incl. Toast, Zebra, allegedly GE, Philips, Shell)
incidents.vector: The Clop extortion group mass-exploited a critical unauthenticated RCE zero-day (CVE-2026-12569) in PTC's Windchill and FlexPLM products, deploying a custom Windchill-specific web shell for credential theft, data theft, and sustained access.
incidents.impact: Clop claims data theft from dozens of organizations, including some of the world's largest publicly traded companies, and began extortion emails in mid-July; the full victim scope is still emerging, echoing prior Clop MOVEit and Oracle EBS campaigns.

incidents.victim: Slovakia national traffic-camera network (279 cameras)
incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found that NERO R-ONE traffic cameras — rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M devices bought via a Cyprus shell company — contain a backdoor that grants shell and network access when triggered by SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, alongside disabled SecureBoot and open unauthenticated live streams.
incidents.impact: 279 cameras were purchased under a €30 million EU-funded project and installed on Slovak roads; deployment was paused pending an independent audit, and similar devices are reportedly installed elsewhere in Eastern Europe.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (transport and urban development departments)
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted email, remote gateways, and internet connectivity across two Berlin city departments; IT staff disconnected the agencies from the city network to contain the incident.
incidents.impact: Operations at the transport and urban development departments were disrupted while systems were isolated to prevent spread.

incidents.victim: Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disabled physical building systems at Manitoba's largest hospital, including access-control doors and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning.
incidents.impact: The hospital increased onsite security while the access-card system was down; it said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Fortune 500 companies (allegedly McDonald's, Vodafone, Gap, Intercontinental, Wyndham)
incidents.vector: A threat actor known as TheHatman claims to have used stolen credentials to access each victim's Microsoft Azure environments and exfiltrate employee data.
incidents.impact: The actor is selling employee data allegedly stolen from almost a dozen Fortune 500 companies; claims are unverified.

incidents.victim: SafePal (hardware crypto-wallet provider)
incidents.vector: Attackers stole customer personal information for everyone who ordered SafePal wallets between March 2, 2025 and April 11, 2026.
incidents.impact: Personal data on 40,000 customers was exposed; no seed phrases or private keys were affected, but the data could enable physical 'wrench' attacks on wallet holders.

incidents.victim: Bits of Gold (Israel's largest cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Data was stolen from an external analytics service provider used by the exchange.
incidents.impact: Data on 250,000 customers was stolen; the company did not specify the data types involved.

incidents.victim: Baylor Genetics (genetics testing company)
incidents.vector: A security breach in June exposed personal information; the specific intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Both patient and employee data were compromised; the company did not disclose the number of affected individuals.

incidents.victim: 144 US universities, 42 US companies, US/state/UN government agencies
incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against professor email accounts and used stolen credentials to access university library systems and corporate/government inboxes, on behalf of the IRGC.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a 14-count indictment charging 17 members; the campaign (2013-2017) stole at least 31.5 terabytes of academic data and intellectual property from 144 US and 178 foreign universities, plus accounts tied to the Department of Labor, FERC, UN organizations, and state agencies. State Department offered up to $10 million rewards for five defendants.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies hiring remote technical staff (software, staffing, healthcare, fintech)
incidents.vector: North Korean IT workers (Recorded Future's 'PurpleDelta'), largely operating from Shenyang, China, used at least 22 fabricated personas backed by AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants, anti-detect browsers, and forged IDs to secure remote jobs, then relied on facilitators and remote-desktop tools to work from company-issued hardware.
incidents.impact: Operators applied to over 1,100 companies (up to 60+ applications/day) and were likely employed at ten or more organizations, posing an active insider threat with earnings funneled to fund the North Korean regime.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: The university took IT systems offline following a security breach detected over the weekend; the intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: UTSA planned to reset all user account passwords once systems were restored and extended tuition payment deadlines; classes were expected to start as scheduled.

incidents.victim: Bluesky and GitHub
incidents.vector: An Iranian hacktivist group known as the 313 Team launched distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks flooding both platforms with junk traffic.
incidents.impact: Bluesky and GitHub suffered prolonged outages over consecutive days; Bluesky said it upgraded its defenses in response.

incidents.victim: Government, critical infrastructure, and healthcare organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Gunra, a Conti-derived ransomware-as-a-service, gains initial access mainly by exploiting known vulnerabilities in internet-facing devices (including Fortinet FortiOS/FortiProxy authentication bypasses CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472) and VPN gateways, using a double-extortion model.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA, and partners issued a joint advisory; Gunra (also operating as 'Golden Community') recruits initial access brokers and has claimed victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific in healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, and other sectors.

incidents.victim: 165+ organizations using Snowflake (incl. AT&T)
incidents.vector: The actor used stolen credentials to access customer Snowflake cloud data environments, then hacked and extorted more than 165 organizations in the 2024 campaign.
incidents.impact: Connor Riley Moucka of Ontario pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy, and admitted stealing call and text records of more than 100 million AT&T customers, in one of the most consequential cybercrime cases of 2024.
